title: Getting Started with draft
text: Writing results section means translating R objects prose, keeping prose accurate time data analysis updates, avoiding errors transcribing values data prose. draft local Shiny app makes process systematic. reads objects R environment, structures values stable named lists, gives live text editor inline references resolve type. ’re done writing, copy two things .qmd .Rmd document: small setup chunk rebuilds lists, inline references like params_m1_$wt$coefficient render correctly every time knit. draft leverages easystats suite packages (https://easystats.github.io/easystats/) systematic consistent structure, relatively dependencies, coverage many different model types analytical approaches R. draft also supports reporting bespoke dataframes create values R environment.

title: Getting Started with draft
text: draft works best alongside easystats packages. Install ones use:
code: # Install from GitHub remotes::install_github("rbcavanaugh/reproducible-reporting") install.packages(c("parameters", "effectsize", "modelbased", "performance", "correlation"))

title: Getting Started with draft
text: workflow three steps: Run analysis normally . Fit models, compute effect sizes, prepare data summaries. Open app calling draft::launch_app(). reads everything current environment. Write copy. Browse objects left panel, write prose editor, copy setup chunk inline references document. Select params_m1 environment panel. inspector shows predictor row copyable chips. Click chip copy path, paste editor, live preview renders value immediately. might write something like: Clicking Copy chunk produces setup code paste document:
code: library(draft) library(parameters)  m1        <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars) params_m1 <- model_parameters(m1)  launch_app() Weight was negatively associated with fuel economy (b = {params_m1_$wt$coefficient}, 95% CI [{params_m1_$wt$ci_low}, {params_m1_$wt$ci_high}], p = {params_m1_$wt$p}). ``` r params_m1_ <- draft::prep_params(params_m1) ```

title: Getting Started with draft
text: model_parameters() main entry point regression models. works consistently across lm, glm, lmer, glmer, brms, many others — output always structure, draft handles way. inline path pattern always list_name_$term$field. Field names vary model type — frequentist models produce coefficient p; Bayesian models produce median pd. inspector always shows exact field names specific model — check rather assuming. Correlation matrices correlation package work , since correlation() returns parameters_model object: app doesn’t control statistics. Confidence levels, standardization, options stay script. use 89% CIs instead 95%: Relaunch app changing script see updated values.
code: library(parameters)  # Linear model params_lm   <- model_parameters(lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars))  # Logistic regression params_glm  <- model_parameters(glm(am ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars, family = binomial))  # Mixed model library(lme4) params_lmer <- model_parameters(lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject),                                      data = sleepstudy), effects = "fixed")  # Bayesian — same workflow, different field names (median, pd instead of coefficient, p) # params_bayes <- model_parameters(brm(...)) library(correlation) corr_matrix <- correlation(mtcars[, 1:4]) # e.g. corr_matrix_$mpg_wt$r, corr_matrix_$mpg_wt$p params_lm_89  <- model_parameters(m1, ci = 0.89) params_lm_std <- model_parameters(m1, standardize = "refit")

title: Getting Started with draft
text: Effect size objects come two shapes depending function. Single-effect functions (e.g. cohens_d(), cramers_v()) return single-row result preps flat named list — path goes directly field: Multi-effect functions (e.g. eta_squared() several predictors) return one row per predictor prep nested list keyed predictor name: Conversion functions like d_to_r() return plain numeric scalars rather effectsize objects. appear environment panel scalar values (see Working scalars ).
code: library(effectsize)  es_d <- cohens_d(mpg ~ am, data = mtcars) # es_d_$cohens_d, es_d_$ci_low, es_d_$ci_high  es_v <- cramers_v(table(mtcars$cyl, mtcars$gear)) # es_v_$cramers_v_adjusted, es_v_$ci_low es_eta <- eta_squared(aov(mpg ~ cyl + gear, data = mtcars)) # es_eta_$cyl$eta2_partial, es_eta_$cyl$ci_low # es_eta_$gear$eta2_partial

title: Getting Started with draft
text: modelbased produces marginal means, contrasts, slopes — prepped named list keyed relevant level comparison. Keys come directly factor level names. Descriptive levels like "control" "treatment" produce readable paths; numeric levels like 4, 6, 8 need backtick-quoting $ paths — inspector handles automatically click chip.
code: library(modelbased)  m <- lm(mpg ~ factor(cyl) + wt, data = mtcars)  # Marginal means — one entry per level means_cyl     <- estimate_means(m, at = "cyl") # means_cyl_$`4`$mean, means_cyl_$`6`$mean  # Contrasts — keys use the _vs_ pattern contrasts_cyl <- estimate_contrasts(m, contrast = "cyl") # contrasts_cyl_$`4_vs_6`$difference, contrasts_cyl_$`4_vs_6`$ci_low  # Marginal slopes m_int      <- lm(mpg ~ wt * factor(cyl), data = mtcars) slopes_wt  <- estimate_slopes(m_int, trend = "wt", at = "cyl") # slopes_wt_$`4`$coefficient, slopes_wt_$`6`$coefficient

title: Getting Started with draft
text: model_performance() returns flat list fit indices single model. compare_performance() returns nested list keyed model name. Available indices depend model type — mixed models include ICC, logistic models include Tjur’s R². inspector shows exactly model provides.
code: library(performance)  perf_lm    <- model_performance(m1) # perf_lm_$r2, perf_lm_$aic, perf_lm_$rmse  comparison <- compare_performance(   m_null <- lm(mpg ~ 1, data = mtcars),   m_full <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl + am, data = mtcars) ) # comparison_$m_full$aic, comparison_$m_full$r2

title: Getting Started with draft
text: datawizard::describe_distribution() produces distribution summary table. draft supports plain (unstratified) stratified (=) forms. Unstratified — one entry per variable, flat list: Stratified — common use: one entry per group, per variable: Multiple variables supported; group keys pasted together _. Note column names dots (Sepal.Length) become compacted keys (sepallength) — check inspector exact key names.
code: library(datawizard)  dist_baseline <- describe_distribution(df[, c("age", "anxiety", "sleep")]) # dist_baseline_$age$mean, dist_baseline_$age$sd # dist_baseline_$sleep$median dist_by_condition <- describe_distribution(   df[, c("age", "sleep", "condition")],   by = "condition" ) # dist_by_condition_$control$age$mean # dist_by_condition_$treatment$sleep$sd

title: Getting Started with draft
text: data.frame tibble environment appears environment panel. draft summarises column automatically: Continuous columns (numeric 10 unique values) — mean, sd, median, min, max, n, n_missing Categorical columns (factor, character, numeric ≤ 10 unique values) — n n_missing overall, plus n pct per level High-cardinality factor/character columns (e.g. subject IDs, free-text) — excluded; meaningful summary copy threshold continuous categorical defaults 10 unique values can adjusted:
code: # prep_data() is what the app calls — you can also call it directly desc_ <- draft::prep_data(mtcars)  # desc_$mpg$mean, desc_$mpg$sd # desc_$cyl$`4`$n, desc_$cyl$`4`$pct desc_ <- draft::prep_data(my_df, cat_threshold = 20)

title: Getting Started with draft
text: single value — numeric, character, logical — assigned variable appears environment panel scalar. setup code needed. Reference directly name prose: Numeric scalars displayed rounded two decimal places. Conversion functions effectsize land :
code: n_participants <- 120 study_site     <- "Pittsburgh"  # {n_participants} participants were recruited from {study_site}. # → 120 participants were recruited from Pittsburgh. es_d   <- cohens_d(mpg ~ am, data = mtcars) d_as_r <- d_to_r(es_d$Cohens_d) # d_as_r appears as a scalar ≈ 0.24

title: Getting Started with draft
text: Everything inside {} evaluated R. limited plain variable names — valid R expression works. report proportion percentage, write {my_value * 100}% editor. examples: {abs(b)} drop sign, {n - 1} degrees freedom, {ifelse(p < .05, "significant", "non-significant")} conditional language. app statistical settings . decisions report — confidence level, effect size type, standardization — live script function arguments. Change relaunch. Check field names inspector. Field names vary model type package version. inspector shows exact names specific object; always check rather relying documentation examples. trailing underscore intentional. prep list params_m1 stored params_m1_. underscore distinguishes original model object prose prevents name collisions. Numeric formatting follows APA style automatically. Non-p values rounded two decimal places scientific notation suppressed. P-values formatted three decimal places < .001 threshold. need round values editor.

title: Interactive Inline Reporting Helper for R Markdown and Quarto
text: app: Environment panel (left) — click params inspect Object inspector (centre) — see formatted parameter estimates copy chips Text editor (right) — write prose like: app suggests params_ list name (object name + trailing underscore). Click Copy inline code — copied text uses `r expr` syntax, ready paste .qmd .Rmd. Click Copy setup chunk — copies prep_params() call put document’s setup chunk. Always re-render full document confirm results reproducible.
code: library(draft)  # 1. Run your analysis in the normal way m1     <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars) params <- parameters::model_parameters(m1)  # 2. Launch the app — it reads everything in your global environment launch_app() Weight was negatively associated with fuel economy (b = {params_$wt$estimate}, 95% CI {params_$wt$ci}, p = {params_$wt$p}).

title: Interactive Inline Reporting Helper for R Markdown and Quarto
text: Converts parameters_model object nested named list inline reporting: parameter sub-list containing available formatted fields: estimate, se, ci, ci_low, ci_high, p (frequentist) pd, rope_pct (Bayesian). Works model class supported parameters::model_parameters(), including correlation matrices.
code: # Setup chunk params_m1 <- parameters::model_parameters(m1) results   <- draft::prep_params(params_m1)  # Inline usage # Weight: b = `r results$wt$estimate` (95% CI `r results$wt$ci`, p = `r results$wt$p`)

title: Interactive Inline Reporting Helper for R Markdown and Quarto
text: Summarises data frame nested named list demographics reporting: Continuous columns return mean, sd, median, min, max, n, n_missing. Categorical columns return n, n_missing, per-level n pct.
code: # Setup chunk stats <- draft::prep_data(demo_data)  # Inline usage # Age: M = `r stats$age$mean` (SD = `r stats$age$sd`) # Female: `r stats$sex$female$pct`%

title: Interactive Inline Reporting Helper for R Markdown and Quarto
text: Converts estimate_means, estimate_contrasts, estimate_slopes objects modelbased package:
code: means_ <- draft::prep_modelbased(modelbased::estimate_means(m1, "cyl")) # `r means_$x4$mean`, `r means_$x6$mean`, `r means_$x8$mean`

title: Interactive Inline Reporting Helper for R Markdown and Quarto
text: Converts model_performance compare_performance output performance package:
code: perf_ <- draft::prep_performance(performance::model_performance(m1)) # R2 = `r perf_$r2`, RMSE = `r perf_$rmse`  comp_ <- draft::prep_performance(performance::compare_performance(m1, m2)) # `r comp_$m1$aic` vs `r comp_$m2$aic`

title: Interactive Inline Reporting Helper for R Markdown and Quarto
text: Converts effectsize_table object (e.g. cohens_d(), eta_squared(), cramers_v()) named list: Single-effect objects return flat list; multi-effect objects (e.g. eta_squared several predictors) return nested list keyed Parameter column.
code: es_ <- draft::prep_effectsize(effectsize::cohens_d(mpg ~ am, data = mtcars)) # `r es_$cohens_d`, 95% CI [`r es_$ci_low`, `r es_$ci_high`]  eta_ <- draft::prep_effectsize(effectsize::eta_squared(aov(mpg ~ cyl + gear, mtcars))) # `r eta_$cyl$eta2`, `r eta_$gear$eta2`

title: Interactive Inline Reporting Helper for R Markdown and Quarto
text: Converts datawizard::describe_distribution() output named list inline reporting: Supports flat (argument) stratified (argument) shapes.
code: dist_ <- draft::prep_distribution(datawizard::describe_distribution(mtcars)) # `r dist_$mpg$mean`, SD = `r dist_$mpg$sd`  # With grouping (by argument): dist_ <- draft::prep_distribution(datawizard::describe_distribution(iris, by = "Species")) # `r dist_$setosa$sepal_length$mean`
